order: The review runner is inherently the Codex driver, but the inert tier and the verification manifest are review POLICY and must bind every review path, including the §5 fallback (in-session review by the Director when Codex is unavailable) and any future engine. - ORCHESTRA.md §8.3: reword the tier as policy — whoever reviews verifies the inertness claim from the diff; the runner enforces it for Codex, a fallback review applies the identical rule by hand. Declare the manifest the canonical command set for every verifier. - ORCHESTRA.md §5: make the fallback review explicitly inherit full review policy — verify tier claims from the diff, judge pasted verification against the manifest, record the tier/depth actually run. - README + runner header: document the policy/transport split.
claims: All three sub-items landed. ORCHESTRA.md §8.3 item 2 rewords the tier as review policy binding whoever reviews, and item 3 declares the `verification` manifest the canonical command set for every verifier. ORCHESTRA.md §5 now carries all three inherited obligations verbatim — verify a declared TIER: inert claim from the diff, judge the executor's pasted verification against the project's `verification` manifest, and record the tier and depth the review actually ran at — so the fallback path is no longer weaker than the Codex path on any of the three. README and the runner header document the policy/transport split. Verified: grepped `manifest` across the changed files and confirmed three hits — ORCHESTRA.md §8.3 item 3, ORCHESTRA.md §5, and the README `verification` bullet — so the manifest obligation is stated on every review path the protocol defines.
